t: Section 47141(f) is amended to read as follows:“(f) Sunset.—This section shall not be in effect after September 30, 2015.”.

fable.w: This section only amends a sunset date for section 47141, setting when that provision stops being in effect. The tempting reading is that the underlying section 47141 might involve outside-party coordination, but the text here contains no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: This section shall not be in effect after September 30, 2015.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a sunset date for a statutory provision, meaning it will cease to be effective after a specific date. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or right to sue mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Section 47141(f) is amended to read as follows:“(f) Sunset.—This section shall not be in effect after September 30, 2015.”

opus.w: This amendment only replaces the sunset clause so that section 47141 stops being in effect after September 30, 2015. Nothing in it brings parties outside the federal government into a federal decision. It could look on-topic because the underlying section concerns State and local governments, but this text sets no consultation, hearing, comment or rulemaking process. Even the underlying grant program would count as an application for benefits, which the definition excludes.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Section 47141 of title 49 deals with grants for State and local land-use planning, so it might seem to involve outside parties. That reading fails because this amendment only sets the date the section stops being in effect. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.

2. **Label:** "No".

qwen_chat.w: This section simply establishes an expiration date for the statute. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before the section ceases to be in effect. The sunset is automatic and does not involve a decision-making process requiring external input.
qwen_chat.s: “(f) Sunset.—This section shall not be in effect after September 30, 2015.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that a "sunset" clause implies a legislative review process where Congress or the public could participate in deciding whether to renew the section. However, the text itself only states the expiration date; it does not mandate any specific consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory committee involvement before the section expires. The expiration is automatic.
